title: S&P Global Flash US PMI (Nov 2026) — 09:45 ET, the date this survey's information actually lands
source: EST: read verbatim off S&P Global's own calendar listing, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, first fetched direct 2026-10-26 and re-fetched direct 2026-11-08 with a browser User-Agent (HTTP 200, 27,453 bytes): 'November 23 ... 14:45 UTC S&P Global Flash US PMI'. 14:45 UTC is 09:45 EST (US clocks changed 2026-11-01). The 2026-10-23 flash, the same series, carries the masthead 'Embargoed until 0945 EDT (1345 UTC) 23 October 2026'. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap for a private PMI compiler, not on date doubt. Checked 2026-11-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-11-08), reading the single prior proposal (proposals/sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-11-23.from-sp-global-manufacturing-pmi-2026-11-02.json) as input. READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT. IMPACT KEPT low ON PURPOSE: the sibling Sep entry was raised to medium on a window that ran above its own median in 11 of 14 instrument-days; re-measured on the current 60-session sample (2026-08-14..11-06) across 08-21 / 09-23 / 10-23 it is 10 of 14, 2 of 14 at or above p90, and direction is still unreadable, so the tier is a cadence knob that would only buy more sessions, not a better call. The flash is the only term of this survey that carries a published consensus; the final carries only the revision, and the last one was large (October composite 57.6 flash -> 55.9 final).
